query: Which material can be used for improve the magnetocaloric properties, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Alloying a base magnetocaloric material with gadolinium will enhance its magnetocaloric properties.
generation.material_initial_state: Base magnetocaloric material (e.g., a manganese-based alloy).
generation.conditions: Room temperature and varying magnetic field strengths.
generation.structural_mediator: Changes in the magnetic ordering and entropy of the material due to the addition of gadolinium.
generation.mechanism: Gadolinium has a high magnetic moment and influences the magnetic phase transitions, which can enhance the magnetocaloric effect.
generation.predicted_outcome: An increase in the magnetocaloric effect, indicated by a higher adiabatic temperature change under an applied magnetic field.
generation.baseline: Magnetocaloric properties of the base material without gadolinium.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis is limited to gadolinium alloying and does not consider other potential alloying elements or combinations.
generation.uncertainty: The exact magnitude of the enhancement is uncertain and may vary based on the specific base material and alloying ratios.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare samples of the base magnetocaloric material with varying concentrations of gadolinium and measure their magnetocaloric properties under controlled magnetic fields.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the gadolinium alloyed samples do not show a statistically significant increase in the magnetocaloric effect compared to the baseline material, the hypothesis is falsified.
